subject: Pricing schedule proration — interpretation of exchange / floor anchoring clause
messages:
From: Eleanor Shaw <eleanor@novuscloud.com>
To: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@novuscloud.com
Date: 2026-06-21T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Clarify proration / anchoring language on pricing schedule

Hi Naomi,

Thanks again for the demo last week. We're moving the order schedule into our procurement queue and a couple of our billing folks flagged an ambiguity in the pricing schedule around the 'exchange / floor anchoring' language. Specifically: if we reclassify usage between SKUs (e.g., move 40% of Project A usage into a new Pilot SKU), does the pricing floor/anchoring rebaseline immediately, or only at annual true-up? Our legal and finance teams read the current redline (attached order_schedule_prorate.xlsx) and worry it could allow per-invoice re-anchoring which would materially change unit economics mid-quarter.

Can you confirm intended behavior and, if needed, propose redline language that limits re-anchoring to controlled scenarios?

I'm attaching the draft order schedule (order_schedule_prorate.xlsx) with example lines that triggered the question. Happy to jump on a quick call if that's easier.

Best,
Eleanor Shaw
Head of Procurement, Novus Cloud
(attachment: order_schedule_prorate.xlsx - spreadsheet)

From: naomi_feldman <naomi@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Shaw <eleanor@novuscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-22T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify proration / anchoring language on pricing schedule

Hi Eleanor,

Thanks for flagging this — good catch. Intent from our side is that the "anchoring" mechanism is designed to protect both parties at annual true-up and during contract renewal, not to force per-invoice rebaselining when customers move volumes across SKUs during normal operations. In other words: mid-term SKU reclassifications shouldn't automatically reset the guaranteed floor.

Proposed immediate next steps:
- I asked Karthik (legal) to draft a concise redline that limits re-anchoring to: (a) material reclassifications (threshold to be defined), and (b) where both parties agree in writing, or at the annual true-up.
- Laura to confirm pricing/ops side if a materiality threshold (e.g., 20-30%) is acceptable.
- Eleanor, if you can confirm whether Novus wants pilot SKUs excluded from re-anchoring (common ask), we can add a carveout.

I've attached our initial markup for context (redline_markup_v1.docx).

Proposed mutual action plan (MAM):
1) Karthik provides redline by EOD tomorrow.
2) Novus comments within 48 hours.
3) Final wording pushed into order form; legal to confirm DocuSign flow.

If that schedule works, I'll track this in the deal (HubSpot link below) and spin up a short call with finance if needed.

Thanks,
Naomi Feldman
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(attachment: redline_markup_v1.docx - Word)

From: karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, Eleanor Shaw <eleanor@novuscloud.com>
Cc: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-23T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify proration / anchoring language on pricing schedule

Eleanor / Naomi —

Thanks — I've drafted suggested redline language below and attached a tracked changes doc for line-insertion. This is intended to be tight and operationally straightforward. Please review and advise.

Suggested clause (for insertion into Exhibit A - Pricing Schedule):
"If Customer reclassifies usage among SKUs such that the Customer's billed quantity for a given SKU changes by more than twenty percent (20%) on a trailing thirty (30) day basis (a \"Material Reclassification\"), the parties shall have the option to re-anchor the applicable pricing floor for the remainder of the then-current Contract Term, provided that any such re-anchoring shall only take effect upon mutual written agreement executed by authorized signatories of both parties. Absent such mutual written agreement, the previously established pricing floor shall remain in effect until the next annual true-up or renewal."

Operational notes / rationale:
- 20% threshold is commonly used to avoid very small volume migrations triggering re-anchors.
- We limit the lookback to 30 days to prevent transient spikes from creating a Material Reclassification.
- Mutual written agreement ensures both sides agree to economics changes and enables a clear audit trail for billing.

If Novus prefers a higher threshold (25-30%) or a different lookback window, we can update. Also recommend adding a clear definition of \"Pilot SKU\" so that short-term pilots (<= 90 days) are excluded from Material Reclassification calculations.

Attachment: redline_markup_v1.docx (contains tracked changes and a proposed footnote for pilot carveout).

- Karthik
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

From: laura_bennett <laura@redwood.com>
To: Eleanor Shaw <eleanor@novuscloud.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi@redwood.com>, karthik_iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-24T16:28:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Clarify proration / anchoring language on pricing schedule

Eleanor — quick note from pricing ops: we can accept the mutual agreement requirement and the 30-day lookback. One tweak request on our side: move the Material Reclassification threshold to twenty-five percent (25%) to better avoid churn in high-velocity accounts, and explicitly carve out Pilot SKUs (<= 90 days) from the calculation.

If Novus agrees to 25% + Pilot carveout, we'll finalize the language and send a DocuSign packet (I'll generate once Karthik updates the markup). Naomi — can you confirm target signature date? Eleanor — if procurement is comfortable, please confirm by EOD Friday so we can meet Novus' internal procurement window.

Laura Bennett
Head of Pricing & Packaging, Redwood Inference
